docs.title: Nations Registry
docs.text:
Welcome to the official registry for the nations of the server.

This site records each nation's public information, including its government, geography, culture, and laws.

docs.title: Nations
docs.text:
Holy Commonwealth of Ardennes

A constitutional religious commonwealth with regional administration, protected lands, private enterprise, and state-guided strategic industries.

Flux Nation

The official public record for Flux Nation, including its government, geography, culture, and independent legal system.

docs.title: About the Registry
docs.text: Each nation controls the content of its own section. National law pages should contain enacted rules only; proposals and drafts should be clearly marked as such. Each nation may organize and number its laws according to its own legal system.

docs.title: Holy Commonwealth of Ardennes
docs.text: Demonym: Ardennian Government: Constitutional Religious Commonwealth Head of State: High Chancellor Spiritual Authority: Grand Hierophant Economic System: State-Guided Capitalism

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Holy Commonwealth of Ardennes is a sovereign nation organized around a strong central government, regional administration, national religious tradition, private enterprise, and public stewardship of strategic resources and protected lands.

Ardennes emphasizes orderly development, engineering, agriculture, cultural continuity, conservation, and national defense.

docs.title: Culture of Ardennes
docs.text: Ardennian culture places strong value on craftsmanship, civic order, architecture, engineering, agriculture, religious tradition, conservation, and national service. Test

docs.title: Religion and Civic Life
docs.text: The national faith influences public ceremony, education, architecture, law, and cultural life. Other religions may be practiced, while the Commonwealth formally supports its national religious institutions.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Ardennian settlements are encouraged to develop recognizable regional character rather than purely functional construction. Public works, monumental buildings, religious structures, civic spaces, and traditional settlement patterns are treated as part of the national identity.

docs.title: Industry and Craft
docs.text: Ardennes is known for precision machinery, engineering, defense production, and high-value agricultural goods.

docs.title: Food and Agriculture
docs.text: Wine is one of Ardennes' notable national products. Vineyards, farms, local markets, cafés, and restaurants are considered important parts of both rural and urban culture.

docs.title: Geography of Ardennes
docs.text: Ardennes contains a mixture of settled heartlands, protected interior territory, forests, agricultural districts, coastlines, islands, volcanic landscapes, and colder northern environments.

docs.title: Ardennian Heartlands
docs.text: The principal population and administrative center of the Commonwealth. It contains the national capital and major urban development.

docs.title: Lower Ardennes
docs.text: A developed southern region with settlements, agriculture, transport links, and commercial activity.

docs.title: Ardennian Interior
docs.text: A largely protected inland region reserved for national parks, wilderness, conservation, and controlled development.

docs.title: Caelorian Archipelago
docs.text:
An island region centered on Caelora. The archipelago includes tropical and volcanic landscapes, protected habitats, and smaller surrounding islands.

Parts of the archipelago fall under national-park and protected-habitat rules.

docs.title: Government of Ardennes
docs.text: Ardennes is a constitutional religious commonwealth with authority divided between national leadership, the judiciary, ministries, and regional governments.

docs.title: High Chancellor
docs.text: The High Chancellor is head of state, chief executive, and commander of the armed forces. The office directs national policy, administration, foreign affairs, and defense.

docs.title: Grand Hierophant
docs.text: The Grand Hierophant is the highest spiritual authority of the Commonwealth and guardian of Sacred Doctrine. The office advises on matters involving national religious tradition, civic life, and institutions of faith.

docs.title: Commonwealth Assembly
docs.text: The Commonwealth Assembly provides regional representation and a formal forum for governors to advise on legislation, development, and national policy.

docs.title: High Court
docs.text: The High Court is the highest judicial body of Ardennes. It interprets national law, resolves major disputes, and reviews questions involving the legal code.

docs.title: Ministries
docs.text:
The Commonwealth may maintain ministries for areas including:

  • Defense
  • Engineering
  • Agriculture
  • Infrastructure
  • Industry and Commerce
  • Energy and Resources
  • Foreign Affairs
  • Culture
  • Land Preservation

docs.title: Regional Government
docs.text: Regions are administered by governors. Regional governments may manage local development and administration, but remain subject to national law and the authority of the Commonwealth government.

docs.title: Legal Code of Ardennes
docs.text: This section contains enacted laws of the Holy Commonwealth of Ardennes.

docs.title: Constitutional & Government Law
docs.text: Rules governing national institutions, public authority, regional administration, and official offices.

docs.title: Civil & Commercial Law
docs.text: Rules governing property, businesses, foreign commercial activity, contracts, and ordinary civic matters.

docs.title: Agricultural & Animal Welfare Law
docs.text: Rules governing farming, livestock, animal welfare, and agricultural practices.

docs.title: Environmental & Protected Lands Law
docs.text: Rules governing national parks, protected habitats, conservation areas, wildlife, and restricted development.

docs.title: Citation Format
docs.text:
Laws should use a short code and sequential number, for example:

  • AC-001 — Agricultural Code, Act 001
  • CC-001 — Civil & Commercial Code, Act 001
  • EC-001 — Environmental Code, Act 001
  • GC-001 — Government Code, Act 001

Individual sections within an act may be cited as §1, §2, §3, and so on.

docs.title: AC-001 — Iron Golem Farming Prohibition Act
§1. Prohibition
docs.text: The construction, operation, or maintenance of farms designed to repeatedly spawn and kill iron golems for industrial resource production is prohibited within the Commonwealth.

docs.title: §2. Scope
docs.text: This prohibition applies to public, private, commercial, and state-operated facilities.

docs.title: AC-002 — Animal Welfare and Livestock Husbandry Act
§1. General Standard
docs.text: Animals kept for agriculture must be provided sufficient usable space, shelter where appropriate, and conditions that do not rely on severe overcrowding or prolonged confinement.

docs.title: §2. Animal Classes
docs.text:
For enclosure standards, animals are grouped into large animals and small animals.

Large animals include cattle, horses, donkeys, llamas, camels, and comparable animals. Small animals include sheep, goats, pigs, chickens, rabbits, and comparable animals.

docs.title: §3. Minimum Space — Large Animals
docs.text: Number of animals Minimum enclosure 1–2 6×6 blocks 3–4 12×12 blocks 5–8 18×18 blocks 9–12 24×24 blocks 13–16 30×30 blocks Each additional 4 +6 blocks to each dimension

docs.title: §4. Minimum Space — Small Animals
docs.text: Number of animals Minimum enclosure 1–2 4×4 blocks 3–4 6×6 blocks 5–8 10×10 blocks 9–12 14×14 blocks 13–16 18×18 blocks Each additional 4 +4 blocks to each dimension

docs.title: §5. Usable Space
docs.text: Buildings, machinery, inaccessible landscaping, or other areas unavailable to the animals do not count toward the minimum enclosure requirement.

docs.title: §6. Breeding and Holding
docs.text: Animals may not be mass-bred or stored in conditions that would violate the normal space and welfare requirements of this act.

docs.title: §7. Transport and Temporary Holding
docs.text: Temporary holding areas may be smaller than permanent enclosures only where the confinement is brief and necessary for transport, sale, veterinary handling, or relocation.

docs.title: §8. Humane Slaughter
docs.text: Methods relying on prolonged suffocation, drowning, burning, entity cramming, or comparable unnecessary suffering are prohibited.

docs.title: AC-003 — Companion and Working Animal Protection Act
§1. Protected Animals
docs.text: Tamed, named, companion, and working animals are protected from deliberate neglect, abandonment, and unnecessary killing.

docs.title: §2. Working Animals
docs.text: Working animals must be provided appropriate resting space when not in active use.

docs.title: §3. Abandonment
docs.text: Owners should make reasonable arrangements for animals they no longer intend to keep rather than leaving them permanently confined or unattended.

docs.title: §1. Foreign Businesses
docs.text: Non-citizens and foreign nationals may establish shops, cafés, restaurants, and other lawful commercial establishments within Ardennes, subject to national and local regulations.

docs.title: §2. Jurisdiction
docs.text: Foreign-owned businesses operating within Ardennes remain subject to Ardennian law while operating inside Commonwealth territory.

docs.title: §3. Property and Development
docs.text: Commercial construction must comply with applicable land-use, architectural, environmental, and regional rules.

docs.title: §4. National Treatment
docs.text: Permission to conduct business does not itself grant citizenship, political office, territorial rights, or exemption from Ardennian law.

docs.title: EC-001 — Protected Lands and Habitat Act
§1. Protected Areas
docs.text: The Commonwealth may designate national parks, protected habitats, ecological reserves, and other conservation areas.

docs.title: §2. Development
docs.text: Construction, extraction, clearing, and industrial activity may be restricted or prohibited within protected areas.

docs.title: §3. Wildlife
docs.text: Wildlife and rare species within protected areas may receive additional protection from unnecessary killing, capture, or habitat destruction.

docs.title: §4. Caelorian Protected Lands
docs.text: Designated portions of the Caelorian Archipelago are protected for ecological, scenic, and scientific value.

docs.title: Constitutional & Government Law
docs.text: This code governs the institutions and public offices of Ardennes.

docs.title: §1. National Authority
docs.text: The Commonwealth government exercises national authority through the High Chancellor, Grand Hierophant, Commonwealth Assembly, High Court, ministries, and other lawfully established offices.

docs.title: §2. Regional Administration
docs.text: Regional governments administer local affairs subject to national law.

docs.title: §3. Public Offices
docs.text:
Additional ministries, commissions, and offices may be established as required for administration of the Commonwealth.

This page is intentionally concise until additional constitutional acts are formally enacted.

docs.title: Laws of Flux Nation
docs.text:
This section is reserved for the official legal system of Flux Nation.

Flux does not need to use the same code, act, numbering, or category system as Ardennes. Its legal pages should reflect the way Flux actually governs and records law.

docs.title: Legal Structure
docs.text:
To be defined by Flux Nation.

Once Flux establishes its system, this page can explain things such as:

  • what types of law or legal instruments exist;
  • who may enact or issue them;
  • how they are numbered or named;
  • which form of law takes precedence;
  • how amendments and repeals are recorded.

docs.title: Current Laws
docs.text:
No laws have been entered into the registry yet.

When Flux defines its legal system, create whatever subpages make sense for it. Examples might include acts, decrees, council decisions, codes, ordinances, charters, or an entirely different structure.
